text:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing intermittent pod-to-pod DNS failures for a headless service (payments/redis-cluster) in us-west-prod starting ~10:04 UTC. Pods on some nodes can't resolve SRV records, other nodes fine.

eric: Ugh. Symptoms? timeouts, NXDOMAIN, or stale IPs?

maya: NXDOMAIN from app logs when it tries to lookup redis-cluster.default.svc.cluster.local (SRV). Curl to podIP works, but service name fails.

jon: Can you paste dig +short and endpointslice list? also kube-proxy logs from affected nodes.

maya: Sure — dig output from an affected pod:
```
$ dig +short SRV _redis._tcp.redis-cluster.default.svc.cluster.local
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> +short SRV _redis._tcp.redis-cluster.default.svc.cluster.local
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
```

maya: kubectl get endpointslices -n payments -l kubernetes.io/service-name=redis-cluster -o wide shows multiple slices but several have 0 addresses on a subset of nodes.

maya: kube-proxy logs on node ip-10-0-5-12: `ipvs sync skipped for service X: endpoints changed but no local endpoints` spam, and conntrack evictions around the same time.

priya: That sounds like kube-proxy isn't seeing the EndpointSlice updates or failing to program iptables/ipvs for those nodes. Could be a race with kubelet churn or conntrack overflow.

eric: Check node-level kube-proxy metrics: endpoint_slice_sync_errors, and conntrack count: `conntrack -S` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`.

maya: conntrack reported high usage on affected nodes (90%). nf_conntrack_max is 65536. We had a burst of job restarts earlier which may have overflowed it.

jon: If conntrack overflowed, kube-proxy could drop connections and also fail to mirror endpoints temporarily until resync. Did rolling restart of kube-proxy help?

maya: We did a quick rolling restart of kube-proxy on the three impacted nodes at 10:22 and service DNS resolved again immediately on those nodes.

priya: Temp fix makes sense. Need root cause: why did conntrack spike? Could be a batch job that created many short-lived connections to pods (sidecars?). We should correlate with autoscaler events and GPU provisioning spikes — I see a scheduled spike at 10:00 for batch trainer jobs.

eric: Proposed mitigations: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max on kernel for prod nodes, 2) tune kube-proxy resync interval or enable brokers to force quicker EndpointSlice reconciliation, 3) add alerts on conntrack usage and endpoint_slice_sync_errors.

jon: Also consider enabling endpoint slice mirroring or reduce ephemeral connection churn via connection pooling in the batch jobs.

maya: Filing a follow-up with infra runbook updates. For the short term I'm going to: bump conntrack to 200k on the node pool template, add an alert at 80% usage, and increase kube-proxy syncPeriod to 15s from 60s for this pool and observe.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-432 — "EndpointSlice / conntrack spike causing headless DNS SERVFAIL". Owner: maya.

eric: Sounds good. Can we also test if CoreDNS caching TTL caused the SERVFAIL propagation? If CoreDNS cached SERVFAIL from failing nodes, other pods might see failures until TTL expired.

maya: Checked coredns logs — it returns SERVFAIL when forward to kube-dns plugin fails to get endpoints. Restarting kube-proxy made kube-dns responses healthy and CoreDNS stopped returning SERVFAIL.

priya: Action items:
- [maya] bump kernel conntrack and roll out via machine image (in progress)
- [eric] add conntrack usage alert and endpoint_slice_sync_errors dashboard (today)
- [jon] load-test headless service with ephemeral connections and validate kube-proxy behavior (this week)
- [infra] draft runbook steps: when headless DNS SERVFAIL -> check endpointslices + conntrack + restart kube-proxy on affected nodes (ASAP)

maya: One note: this only impacted headless (SRV) lookups — ClusterIP services were OK because kube-proxy had local endpoints for them. Might be related to how kube-proxy mirrors EndpointSlices for headless services.

eric: OK. I'll open a postmortem once we have metrics and timelines. Thanks for the quick fix :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks all, monitoring now.
